step2.body: GitRaptor keeps restore points. One button takes you back.

step3.body: If an agent tries to delete or rewrite your main branch, it's stopped and explained.

detail.gone: This pair is no longer predicted.

block.attemptedPush: A {{kind}} of {{source}} onto {{ref}} on the server ({{remote}}), at {{time}}.

do.exception: If you're the one who needs it, you can make an exception for this once.
do.nothing: Nothing: protection did its job. You can tell the agent to use another branch.

block.nothing: Nothing happened. {{ref}} is unchanged on your machine and on the server.
block.nothingLocal: Nothing happened. {{ref}} is unchanged on your machine.
block.title: Blocked: {{actor}} tried to {{operation}}
block.titleNoActor: Blocked: someone tried to {{operation}} (no agent identified)

why.deletebase: It deletes your main branch, the starting point for everyone.
why.forcepush: It replaces the server's history. Commits others pushed that aren't on your machine would be lost for everyone.

grd.empty: Nothing blocked in {{repo}}. Protection is on.

exc.branchDeleteHint: If git says the branch isn't merged and you still want to delete it, change -d to -D.
exc.cancelHow: Once you run it you have 10 seconds to cancel: press Ctrl-C in that terminal.
exc.cancelOr: Or run this in another terminal:
exc.cancelled: Cancelled: nothing ran. It's in the log.
exc.engineDown: The engine is stopped: the exception needs it.
exc.mismatch: The announced exception isn't the one you copied: cancel it with Ctrl-C in that terminal.

notOffered.commit: The exception only works for push, deleting a local branch and rebase.
notOffered.operation: The exception only works for push, deleting a local branch and rebase.
notOffered.raptorUnknown: GitRaptor can't find its own `raptor` to write the command.
notOffered.rateLimited: GitRaptor didn't log where it happened, so it can't write the command.
notOffered.remote: The exception needs a remote by name, not a URL.
notOffered.rule: This rule can't be skipped with an exception.
notOffered.unsafeText: A name in this operation has characters that could act on your terminal, so we don't offer the command.
notOffered.whereUnknown: GitRaptor didn't log where it happened, so it can't write the command.

exc.pending: Exception announced in a terminal: runs in {{n}} s
exc.reason: This version of GitRaptor can't ask for Touch ID yet, so the confirmation happens in your terminal.
exc.rebaseHint: GitRaptor doesn't log which base the agent rebased onto, so it can't write the command for you. If you really need it, write it in your terminal after `--` and read what it shows before accepting.
exc.remote: GitRaptor can't undo this on the server: it may delete other people's commits.
exc.review: Check the command: the terminal shows what it will do and asks before doing it. If the terminal shows `--yes` or a different operation, cancel it.
exc.sourceInferred: Inferred source branch: {{branch}} (the one checked out in that folder when it was blocked). Check in the terminal's plan that it's the one you want to push.
exc.terminal: To prove it's you and not an agent, run this command in your own terminal (not an agent's):
exc.terminal.title: Confirm from your terminal
exc.where: Where's the terminal? Press Cmd+Space and type "Terminal".
exc.who: You do it, not {{agent}}. It runs once; the rule stays on afterwards.

gloss.exception: Doing, once and on record, something the protection blocks.
gloss.forcePush: Push to the server replacing its history. It can delete other people's work.
gloss.hooks: Small programs Git runs before some operations; that's how risky ones are stopped.
gloss.protection: Rules that stop dangerous Git operations in this repo.

op.forcePush: rewrite the history of {{ref}} on the server ({{remote}})
